requirements.text: Node Graph tab must show graph-patch lineage: superseded nodes remain visible and clickable for historical detail, patched generations branch from the old path, and the live path may rejoin surviving downstream nodes.

Seams tab is hierarchical: top level Feature Seams, second level Work Packages, with nodes appearing as drill-in summaries; detail panel emphasizes governance/completion/integration truth rather than raw node execution churn.

Node Graph tab provides a graph canvas plus right-side detail inspector exposing requested/effective provider/model/effort/persona/account, usage/token/cost, worker policy, retry/review/promotion state, lane/worktree/snapshot state, and linked evidence/artifacts; evidence/artifact links deep-link to the Evidence tab with target selection/filter applied.

Evidence tab uses separate panes: Evidence pane (verdicts/receipts/findings/reports) and Artifacts pane (screenshots/recordings/diffs/reports/generated docs); the two remain bidirectionally linked, with usage-linked receipts when relevant.

Right-side inspectors stay summary/action oriented; dense objects (attempt handoff artifacts, review records, corroboration records, graph patch requests, state transition reports, promotion records, recovery records) open full-record views.

Weak Integration must be summarized visibly in Seams under readable headings (Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, Design); package issues roll up to seam concerns only when they cross package/seam/user-visible boundaries or affect seam completion truth.

Blocked states must always expose blocked reason, blocked owner, time blocked, and next step; blocked ownership uses stable labels (Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, External Resource).

Alert levels separate into Info, Warning, Attention, Action Required; Dashboard surfaces summary/urgency, Orchestrator surfaces detailed operational alert context, and chat-thread is reserved for situations that actually need user resolution/decision.
Tab badges stay sparse and purposeful: Progress badge represents meaningful attention/action-required count; other tabs prefer targeted counts or simple dot-badges over noisy unread-like counters.

Orchestrator widgets consume stable shared projections rather than raw event streams or bespoke queries; the widget shell needs widget identity/type, scope, filter/sort/display config, and a projection ref.
Each tab needs role-appropriate filters; Orchestrator must support saved views (at least per project) covering tabs, filters, sort, grouping, and widget layout.
Override display must explicitly show Inherited, Overridden, and Effective values without requiring a separate modal to understand resolution/inheritance/fallback.

Any provider-using actor (assistant chat, interviewer, requirements-doc builder, overseers, node workers, delegated workers) must participate in the same pre-send and post-send account-health loop; completed interactions can update account health and route the next message/attempt to a different account.

Each failed node attempt leaves a structured receipt/handoff artifact (what was done, what changed, why it failed/blocked, what to try next); default retry uses a fresh agent/subagent under policy-driven budgets/caps; some failures route to remediation, graph patch, or block/HITL instead of plain retry.

GUI exposes execution-policy controls: fresh vs same-context retry worker (default fresh), subagents-by-default for nodes with override to full agents, overseer delegation on/off, delegated-worker provider/model/effort policy, and consistent requested-vs-effective identity across chat actors and orchestration actors; worker kind and retry-context are separate settings.

Node personas auto-select from node work/type with a global node-worker-policy override (not per-node); feature seam, work package, and node each carry independent provider/model/effort settings with defaults plus overrideability.

Settings define whether work-package overseers may spawn subagents for node work; if enabled, those subagents' provider/model/effort must be configurable; package-based worktrees are preferred over per-node at expected scale, with explicit lane/ordering rules so dependent nodes inside the same package see correct upstream state.

Worktrees must be visible in the Orchestrator page and likely in Source Control; orchestrator-managed worktrees are partitioned from user-/assistant-created worktrees; multiple projects/repos run Orchestrator concurrently with per-project data/storage isolation, settings, themes, and snapshots.

Multi-account execution must allow switching to another account on usage exhaustion or predicted imminent exhaustion, modeling account/provider selection as requested-vs-effective runtime identity persisted at attempt level.

Add explicit effective_account_id and switch/fallback reason to attempt/runtime visibility; multi-account policy supports cooldown and retry-budget concepts on top of threshold/priority; account selection operates over a provider+role+namespace/pool snapshot; browser-based relogin and log parsing remain optional/supplemental—not canonical quota truth or the default execution model.

decisions.text: Orchestrator remains tab-first (not widget-first); Progress remains the first tab and is the tab that hosts Orchestrator widgets.
Replace the existing Tiers tab with a seam/package-oriented tab (likely Seams).

Keep tabs separate: Progress, Seams (replacement for Tiers), Node Graph, Evidence, History, Ledger; Progress is the widget-hosting operational summary tab; History and Ledger remain separate (chronological story vs. structured durable record inspection).

Default Progress-widget drill targets are deterministic: Run Status -> History; Current Activity / Attention / Worktree Lanes -> Node Graph; Seam Health / Package Activity / Overseer Activity -> Seams; Promotion Queue -> Ledger; Account/Usage Pressure -> Usage; Recent Major Events / Throughput -> History; Corroboration Queue / Recovery State -> Evidence.

Condition aging: unresolved conditions stay on operational surfaces; resolved fall back to History; recently resolved major items may linger briefly; default lifetimes ~15 minutes for normal resolved operational items and up to 24 hours (or until dismissed) for major resolved items; future control is policy-level, not per-alert micro-configuration.
Projection freshness: event-driven updates are the primary model; manual refresh / tab re-open refresh remain secondary; conceptual projection-health states are current, refreshing, stale, failed.
Default sort orders: Seams = most operationally problematic first; History = newest first; Ledger = newest first.

Surface split: Dashboard = summary/urgency/entry points; Orchestrator = operational depth; Projects = multi-project summary/management richer than a tiny status list but still summary-first; Project cards show compact orchestrator/attention/usage pressure and one primary blocked owner/reason when blocked.

New multi-account failover/account-threshold/effective-account behavior extends the existing Usage model and projections; do not invent a second independent account-pressure or quota subsystem beside Usage.

Conversational actors (assistant, interviewer, requirements-doc builder, PRD builder) share provider/account/usage/runtime identity with orchestration actors but are not orchestration nodes/packages/seams; the broader handoff chain runs requirements-doc builder -> interview flow -> PRD builder -> graph-plan inputs -> Orchestrator with human review at document-production stages; Orchestrator-style chat-thread resolution is not projected backward onto ordinary conversational interaction.
Separate task state / completion truth, append-only execution learnings, and reusable pattern memory; do not rely on one giant conversational thread as the only continuity mechanism.

Canonical handoff/retry memory must be structured runtime records (not loose markdown logs); worker-facing handoff is a synthesized bounded packet assembled from canonical records, not full raw history.

New orchestration artifacts (node retry memory, attempt handoff artifacts, reusable learning records, worker handoff packets) map onto the documented stack: event/source-of-truth aspects in seglog, projected/current-state aspects in redb, JSON/JSONL only as user-requested export/inspection; loose JSON files must not be canonical.
Hybrid graph+tier is acceptable only if graph execution remains canonical and tiers become a derived human-facing lens; it is dangerous if both retain execution authority.

Keep the canonical graph as execution truth; introduce bounded coherent subgraph groupings (work packages); assign local overseers to work packages; keep the global Orchestrator runtime deterministic and above those overseers.

Governance layering reintroduces both work-package overseer and same-feature-seam overseer over graph-based execution; feature seam is first-class; weak integration means the feature seam is not complete (package completion is necessary but not sufficient).

System is fully automated by default; HITL is configurable but off by default; on critical failure or major decision, surface the issue in Dashboard, Orchestrator, and a spawned chat-window agent/thread, with chat presenting the issue/decision for resolution.

Lifecycle is per-entity (node, work package, feature seam, promotion, worktree lane) rather than one universal status enum; transitions are deterministic and event-driven; canonical event naming is shared across runtime and UI projections—Orchestrator must not invent a shadow event language.

data_shapes.text: Core Progress-tab widget catalog: Run Status, Current Activity, Attention/Blockers, Seam Health, Package Activity, Promotion Queue, Worktree Lanes, Account/Usage Pressure, Recent Major Events, Overseer Activity, Corroboration Queue, Recovery State, Throughput/Capacity (err on side of more options; user can disable/hide).
Promotions are visible as explicit named boundaries: Lane to Package, Package to Seam, Seam Completion.
Canonical event families remain stable: seam.*, package.*, node.*, promotion.*, corroboration.*, graph_patch.*, recovery.*, account.*.

Concern is a first-class record carrying identity, scope, severity, category, owner, lifecycle state, meaning/summary, linkage to evidence/artifacts/history/source records, and visibility/attention flags; lifecycle states include active, acknowledged, resolved, dismissed.

Required orchestrator projection families: Run Summary, Seam Summary, Package Summary, Node Summary, Promotion Summary, Lane/Worktree Summary, Concern Summary, Account/Usage Pressure, Recent Major Events, Corroboration Summary, Recovery Summary, Overseer Activity.

Settings groupings: Providers & Models, Execution Identity, Governance, Workers, Recovery, HITL; settings-scope hierarchy: App/Global, Project (main execution policy owner), Seam (feature-level overrides), Package (local execution/recovery overrides), Node (rare targeted override), Actor/Role (cross-cutting policy), Runtime only (computed truth, not user configuration).

Documented persistence stack: seglog = canonical append-only event source; redb = durable KV state / checkpoints / projections / rollups; Tantivy = search index; JSONL mirror = disposable projector output, not canonical truth; FinalGUISpec aligns persistence(events)=seglog and layout/settings/state=redb.

Each attempt should produce at minimum: what was attempted, what changed/artifacts produced, checks/tests/review outcome, why it failed/blocked, contamination/restore state if relevant, recommended next action, and reusable learnings/patterns when appropriate.

Canonical persisted objects include at least project, run, feature_seam, work_package, node, attempt, lane, snapshot, promotion, review, resolution_thread, and event; dashboard/orchestrator/source-control summaries are projections, not separate truths.
attempt persists identity, actor type, requested-vs-effective provider/model/effort/persona/account, resolution/fallback metadata, lane/snapshot linkage, lifecycle/result, and evidence refs.
lane persists project/package linkage, worktree binding, lifecycle, contamination state, safe-point linkage, ancestry, and ownership/display grouping for UI separation.
promotion persists promotion class, source/target linkage, eligibility/blocking/HITL state, decision/result, and evidence/review/corroboration linkage.
review persists scope, review type, actor linkage, verdict/severity/blocking, findings, evidence, and timestamps.
resolution_thread persists trigger linkage, resolution kind, issue summary, allowed actions, status, and UI/chat linkage.

Parent objects: project owns identity, repo/project settings/theme/account-policy linkage, active-run pointers, coarse status; run owns execution-session identity/lifecycle, graph linkage, run-level settings snapshot, active pointers/rollup posture; feature_seam owns membership, lifecycle, requested settings, overseer/governance state, seam-promotion state, evidence linkage; work_package owns membership, lifecycle, requested settings, overseer/delegation/worktree policy refs, baseline lane state, package-governance state, promotion linkage, evidence linkage.

routing_rules.text: Orchestrator widgets live inside Progress; some Orchestrator widgets may also be hostable on Dashboard; non-Orchestrator widgets are not hostable on the Orchestrator page; widgets remain resizable/customizable but tab-first structure remains primary.

Cross-tab navigation is a real contract: object/event focus deep-links across Progress / Seams / Node Graph / Evidence / History / Ledger; deep links carry selection/filter/focus context; Seams and Node Graph share focus context without hyperactive live-sync.

Operator visibility splits events into history-only, badge-worthy, attention-card-worthy, and chat-thread-worthy action-required; backbone user-facing events include block/completion/reopen/supersede, promotion blocked/promoted/revoked, graph_patch requested/applied/generation_updated, restore required/failed/completed, threshold crossed/account switched/account exhausted.

Canonical concerns are minted by runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcome, and graph-patch/state-transition logic; workers may nominate findings but must not mint canonical concerns directly; concerns update/escalate/downgrade rather than duplicate.

All major surfaces project the same concern model: Progress = operational attention projection; Seams = integration/governance projection; Evidence = proof-backed concern projection; History = concern lifecycle timeline projection; Ledger = exact structured concern-record projection.

User-facing concern actions stay narrow (open/focus, open evidence/history/ledger, acknowledge/dismiss where allowed, open resolution thread, approve/reject only at true HITL boundaries); runtime/overseer actions (request corroboration, route to remediation, request graph patch, severity/owner mutation, merge/split, true resolution) remain mostly non-generic GUI buttons.

Run Summary, Seam Summary, Concern Summary, Account/Usage Pressure, and Recent Major Events projections are broadly reusable across Orchestrator/Dashboard/Projects; more operational/dense summaries stay primarily Orchestrator-facing.

Under stale projections, degrade from summary/projection surfaces to direct record-backed inspection; Ledger and direct record views become the trust anchor; only certain current/generation-matched direct records support action.

Quota/pressure detection uses heterogeneous signal sources—runtime outcomes, provider capabilities, and (where necessary) log-derived heuristics; usage stays project-scoped with multi-project aggregation as a separate later concern; provider-specific browser auth/manual rotation/log parsing are optional supplemental capabilities, not the canonical execution model.

Orchestrator concerns split into page IA/widget behavior/data bindings vs. execution policy/scheduler consumption/remediation behavior; these must not drift apart, and shadow ownership at the page layer must be removed in favor of consuming canonical contracts.

verification_rules.text: Seam completion is presented distinctly from package completion and from package-to-seam availability using Locally Complete, Available to Seam, and Seam Complete.
Revocation/reopen semantics are explicit and visible: Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, Reopened by New Evidence.

Alert-state semantics: resolved means the underlying condition actually changed; dismissed means presentation hidden/acknowledged while the condition may still exist; active blockers must not be dismissible in a way that makes the system appear unblocked.
Acknowledged is distinct from resolved and dismissed and is intended for advisory/minor/non-blocking concerns; blockers requiring real action must not be acknowledgeable in place of resolution.
Concern resolution must track underlying truth changes, not mere presentation changes.

When projection health undermines trust in blocked/promotion/recovery/patch/account-pressure truth it must mint a real concern; actions that change execution/promotion/recovery/approval truth require fresh-enough projection state, with UI explaining inline what is stale, why it matters, and what to do next; observational/navigation/export actions remain safe under degraded projections.

Event-driven wakeups are the authoritative execution/update model; worktree-native isolation is required; file-lease orchestration is explicitly rejected; blocked outcomes, remediation lineage, retry/backoff posture, and same-cycle reconsideration are first-class orchestration behavior.

Packet emission must not proceed until target-level survivor/stale token contradictions in packet-planning inputs are repaired; current packet artifacts are useful as planning state but are not yet faithful-emission-safe.

Direct-record action surfaces (promotion, graph-patch + state-transition, recovery/restore, concern records) must explicitly show currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, and actionable yes/no before allowing action.

owner_consumer_obligations.text: Working ledger is execution memory only—non-canonical and must not be cited in planning docs; do not write planning-doc changes during work-item stewardship; do not treat the ledger file as packet content, reconciliation text, or canonical cleanup output; preserve packetized state and run metadata while refreshing mode-contract durability files.
Inspector vs full-record split: side inspectors stay summary/action-light; heavy/high-consequence actions and dense records belong in full-record views.
Remove 'optional JSON' wording from design language unless JSON export is explicitly about manual inspection/export; orchestrator-page exportability is desirable but JSON is not canonical storage.

Orchestrator must consume canonical runtime fields and event names from shared contracts; it must not redefine schemas, event types, or live-status mappings locally—those belong to upstream owners (Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md).
Page-layer documents must not retain shadow event/schema ownership: page doc must bind to upstream owners rather than naming concrete event sources or local live-status mappings.

stale_retirement_items.text: Retire vague term 'delegated worker' in favor of 'overseer-spawned node worker' across docs, settings, and runtime contracts.

Retire or derive the first-class tier hierarchy (Phase/Task/Subtask/Iteration) where graph is canonical—Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, Plans/Run_Graph_View.md, and Plans/FinalGUISpec.md still preserve tier vocabulary alongside graph nodes; reconcile shadow event/schema ownership (PuppetMasterEvent::*, named 'Overseer' role) at the page layer with the consumer-of-contracts stance.

Tier-driven orchestration identity, UI labels, and persona defaults retained as first-class overlays over graph nodes are stale—docs must be simplified to graph-native vocabulary with tiers as a derived human lens at most.

open_questions.text: Final canonical name for the Tiers-replacement tab (Seams vs. equivalent) is still open.
Whether History and Ledger should ultimately merge remains on the table (current direction keeps them separate).

Concrete storage medium and worker delivery for handoff/retry artifacts (literal JSON/JSONL vs redb-backed records, project-scoped paths/storage domains, inline-prompt vs referenced-artifact vs fetched-context vs mixed model) is still an open design seam.
Concrete mapping of node retry memory, attempt handoff artifacts, reusable learning records, and worker handoff packets onto seglog/redb shapes is not yet nailed down.
Key unresolved design seam: what is the governing intelligence/control loop in a graph-canonical system (single overseer agent versus bounded packages with local overseers)?

Governance safeguard proposal: when an overseer flags missing work/wiring/design issues, spawn two additional subagents to validate the concern before remediation or graph-change action—implementation depth is open.
Snapshot/safe-point policy and its explicit relationship to the plan graph remains queued for deeper design.
Next subtopic: classify which events are runtime-internal vs operator-visible vs chat-thread resolution events, and define the event model that drives lifecycle transitions.

process_defects.text: packet_plan.json contains at least four survivor/residue contradictions where the same token appears in both required-survivor and stale-retire sets: Plans/Executor_Protocol.md#5. Node execution fields -> TierContext, tier_id; Plans/GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md#Token handling and storage (hard rules) -> github_api:github.com/<login>; Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md#Canonical Runtime Recovery Command Consolidation (2026-03-09) -> approve_continue; Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md#Tier-Level Subagent Strategy -> tier_id.

GUI/spec gaps: no documented surface for work_package or feature_seam yet; no seam-level acceptance/weak-integration/corroboration review affordance; worktree visibility/controls are not coordinated across Orchestrator and Source Control; orchestrator-owned vs non-orchestrator worktrees lack explicit partitioning/filtering; per-project aggregation on dashboard/projects surfaces is unclear.

doc_hints.text: Prefer canonical terms in docs and runtime: tab/object labels Seams, Feature Seam, Work Package, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer; user-facing state/action labels include Locally Complete, Seam Complete, Completion Blocked, Weak Integration, Promotion Blocked, Promotion Revoked, Corroboration Requested, Challenge Accepted/Not Accepted, Advisory Concern Recorded, Graph Patch Requested/Applied, Generation Updated; keep expert/canonical terms stable in docs and derive simpler labels later only for the more technical/loaded ones.

Plans/usage-feature.md is the strongest current owner for usage/quota/alerts/analytics/product-shape; Plans/storage-plan.md and Plans/FinalGUISpec.md carry meaningful usage/runtime/event/GUI assumptions—usage is already a first-class cross-surface concern.

Existing usage docs already assume configurable warning thresholds, platform quota visibility, rate-limit / reset countdown surfaces, project-scoped usage storage, dashboard widgets, orchestrator/runtime event persistence, and usage+ledger+analytics rollups—new multi-account/account-pressure work must extend this rather than duplicate it.

Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md owns the UI/page-shell for the six-tab Orchestrator; Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md treats Orchestrator as the primary consumer of canonical runtime scheduler contracts, executes headless from .puppet-master/project/plan_graph/index.json and node shards, and dispatches from a global ready set.
Direct repo search found no current references to feature seam or work package in Plans/**; current GUI/spec docs do not yet reflect these newly discussed governance objects.

Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md still defines tabs Progress/Tiers/Node Graph Display/Evidence/History/Ledger and says runs/tier checks are driven by 'Overseer'; Plans/Run_Graph_View.md still uses tier-type iconography and tier vocabulary; Plans/FinalGUISpec.md still references phase/task/subtask progress and mapping editors—docs are not yet purely graph-native.

shard-0001: Working ledger explicitly excluded as packet content, reconciliation text, or canonical cleanup output (lines 25-26).
Planning-doc changes excluded during work-item stewardship (line 24).
shard-0003: Browser auto-relogin excluded as a core cross-provider assumption; only optional provider-specific recovery (lines 171-172).
Log parsing excluded as canonical quota truth; supplemental heuristic only (lines 173-174, 178-180).
Manual 'set active' excluded as the main execution model; remains operator/debug control only (line 174).
shard-0004: Deep redesign of existing Orchestrator tab structure excluded from this thread—current spec is weak and not the focus (line 51).
OpenCode-as-provider excluded as a primary target for multi-account support (line 178 of shard-0003 context confirmed here in continuity).
